# Audit of ADAMS_PUSHFORWARD_NO_GO.md (+ literature + the open door)

## Part 1 — The Adams-pushforward no-go: re-derivation and verdict

**Setup.** L is the rank-p root local system on U = P^1_t \ {+1,-1,∞}. The pointwise Adams operation ψ^p satisfies Tr(F_t | (ψ^p L)_t) = Tr(F_t^p | L_t) (raise Frobenius eigenvalues to the p-th power). The doc compares RΓ_c(U, ψ^p L) (Adams before pushforward) with ψ^p RΓ_c(U, L) (Adams after pushforward).

**APN.1 — CONFIRMED.** ψ^p L is a Weil complex on U; Grothendieck-Lefschetz over k=F_Q gives Tr(F | RΓ_c(U_bar, ψ^p L)) = Σ_{t∈U(F_Q)} Tr(F_t | (ψ^p L)_t) = Σ_{t∈U(F_Q)} Tr(F_t^p | L_t). This is a textbook application of the trace formula to the sheaf ψ^p L; the pointwise Adams identity is used correctly. Verified numerically (constant sheaf, Part A below).

**APN.2 — CONFIRMED.** Adams on the cohomology (a virtual Weil module over the point) gives Tr(F | ψ^p RΓ_c(U,L)) = Tr(F^p | RΓ_c(U_bar,L)). Since F = Frob_Q, F^p is the geometric Frobenius of F_{Q^p}; Grothendieck-Lefschetz for the p-th power of Frobenius gives Σ_{t∈U(F_{Q^p})} Tr(F^p | L_t) = Σ_{t∈U(F_{Q^p})} Tr(F_t^p | L_t). The integrand Tr(F^p|L_t) is identical to APN.1's; ONLY the index set differs (U(F_Q) vs U(F_{Q^p})). The cyclic cross-check in §3 is also correct: fixed points of Frob_Q∘τ on U^p are exactly (t, Ft, …, F^{p-1}t) with F^p t = t, i.e. t∈U(F_{Q^p}), reproducing APN.2 — this is the same mechanism by which L-functions carry the Σ N_m T^m/m structure. Verified numerically.

**APN.3 (the obstruction) — CONFIRMED.** The difference is Σ_{t∈U(F_{Q^p})\U(F_Q)} Tr(F_t^p|L_t), a sum over ~Q^p−Q points spread across the entire degree-p extension of the open curve. It is genuinely global and cannot be localized at the finitely many ramification points {±1,∞}. Therefore no O(p) boundary/ramification-supported correction can identify RΓ_c(U,ψ^p L) with ψ^p RΓ_c(U,L). The 'swap the order of Adams and pushforward to shrink the exponential object to something O(p)' shortcut is genuinely dead. This is a real theorem-level obstruction to THAT route (not a proof the crown is false — the doc is careful about this).

**Numeric sanity (exact, p=5,7,11,13).** Toy L = constant Q_l on U (3 rational punctures): H^0_c=0, dim H^1_c=2 (eigenvalues 1), H^2_c=Q_l(-1). Lefschetz: Tr(F|RΓ_c) = Q−2 = #U(F_Q) (APN.1 RHS) ✓; Tr(F^p|RΓ_c) = Q^p−2 = #U(F_{Q^p}) (APN.2 RHS) ✓; difference = Q^p−Q ✓ (global, matches the extension-point sum). All matched exactly. ## Part 2 — Literature (all retrieved via alphaXiv unless noted)

- **Pink–Rössler, arXiv:0812.0254**, 'On the Adams–Riemann–Roch theorem in positive characteristic' — RETRIEVED. Proves p-th ARR for a smooth projective morphism X→Y with Y regular, quasi-projective over F_p, in algebraic (coherent/vector-bundle) K-theory. The doc's characterization is ACCURATE, and it is applied only to say it does NOT transplant to constructible ℓ-adic Weil sheaves — correct: the hypotheses (coherent K-theory, Bott cannibalistic classes) are not met by a constructible local system's compact-support pushforward, so the doc is not misapplying it — it is (correctly) declining to apply it.
- **Maxim–Schürmann, arXiv:1602.06546**, 'Plethysm and cohomology representations of external and symmetric products' — RETRIEVED. Generating-series/character formulae for virtual cohomology representations of external products of constructible/coherent complexes. The doc's claim is ACCURATE: it produces external powers on U^p and its cyclic fixed-point formula sums over U(F_{Q^p}) — i.e. it AGREES with APN.2, so it cannot yield the base-field sum APN.1. Correctly characterized.
- **Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich / Euler–Poincaré** — CONFIRMED via arXiv:0905.1753 (GOS computes the ℓ-adic Euler–Poincaré number on a curve via rank + Swan). Used correctly in the hook ledger: χ_c(U_bar,V_i) = −rank − Swan_∞ on the three-punctured line (only the wild point at ∞ contributes; tame transpositions at ±1 do not). Within hypotheses.
- **Katz — rigid local systems / middle convolution / Airy sheaves** — the framework is CONFIRMED real: middle convolution (Dettweiler–Reiter, arXiv:math/0305311), Airy sheaves as ℓ-adic local systems on A^1 (arXiv:2111.02256 generalizing Katz), rigid connections (arXiv:2603.09252, 2405.18268). Katz's two books (Rigid Local Systems; Exponential Sums and Differential Equations) and Köck 1998 (Ann. Sci. ENS, equivariant GRR) are pre-arXiv/non-arXiv and were NOT directly retrieved, but they are standard, correctly cited, and not load-bearing for the no-go itself.

## Part 3 — The open door: is it real?

**(a) Genuinely not closed by the no-gos — CONFIRMED.** The three no-gos each attack a DIFFERENT object: (i) Cyclic Airy pre-cohomology builds Λ_p as an effective object before cohomology (exponential 2^(p-1) lower bound); (ii) the Adams-pushforward no-go audited here concerns commuting Adams through the SAME-space t-pushforward (global extension-point discrepancy); (iii) root-cover Koszul descent tries to descend a contractible complex from the root cover (generic off-diagonal failure). The surviving claim is about the POST-pushforward q-line Frobenius modules H_even(q)=⊕_{i even}H^1_c(U_bar,V_i), H_odd(q)=⊕_{i odd}H^1_c(U_bar,V_i) — whether their common semisimple Frobenius constituents cancel to leave O(p). No no-go touches these objects; there is no logical closure. The underlying ledger is exact (verified p=5,7,11,13): total rank = 2^(p-1); total H^1_c = ((2p-3)2^(p-1)+3)/p; even and odd each ~2^(p-2); virtual difference exactly 4−p (linear). So a real (not merely virtual/Grothendieck-group) even↔odd Frobenius-eigenvalue cancellation of all but O(p) is exactly what is unresolved. The C_p-invariant closed form (C(p-1,i)+(p-1)(-1)^i)/p was independently confirmed against brute subset-sum counts for p≤11.

**(b) Decidable in principle by Katz-style rigidity / middle convolution — REASONABLE but UNPROVEN.** The hooks ∧^i Std are irreducible pairwise-nonisomorphic S_p local systems arising from the root cover / rank-2 Airy via convolution — squarely inside Katz's category. Middle convolution and rigidity are the correct tools for computing cohomology of and isomorphisms between such objects, so it is the right toolbox and the door is a well-posed target on the correct object ('after fixed-q pushforward' is genuinely essential — no O(p) mechanism survives before pushforward). But 'could in principle decide' is an honest hedge, not a result: whether the parity-reversing correspondence with O(p) unpaired vanishing cycles actually EXISTS is open, and nothing retrieved settles it.

**Ruling: the door is real.** The Adams-pushforward no-go is a correct, exact obstruction that closes one specific shortcut without touching the surviving post-pushforward cancellation claim. The overall document stack is epistemically honest — it does not overclaim the no-gos into a disproof of the crown, and the crown remains genuinely open.
